html:
SMTO-FIL-0019 — SMTO can't do that file action in this way

GUID: 595aeb4a-b793-43cc-ba96-52a9292c9fd1
Slug: file-operation-not-supported
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • SMTO asked for a file action it can't carry out safely, such as copying a folder over an existing folder, replacing a folder during a move, or renaming a file inside a set of edits. This step changed nothing.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you were copying or moving a folder onto one that already exists, ask SMTO to copy it into a new, empty folder instead. SMTO can replace single files, but it can't merge one folder into another.
  2. If SMTO was renaming a file as part of a set of edits, ask it to rename that file as its own separate step. Renames aren't supported inside a set of edits, but a separate move step is.
  3. If a simple move still fails, ask SMTO to copy the file to the new place. Check the copy, then ask SMTO to delete the original. Some drives can't rename safely without risk of replacing a file; copying avoids that.

What success looks like

  • The copy, move or rename finishes and the items are where you expected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the name of the computer and drive involved, to the person who manages the Gateway. Don't treat this step as done; nothing was copied, moved or renamed by it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gateway file operation requested behavior outside the supported implementation: overwrite involving a non-regular source or destination (directory merge), move overwrite of a non-regular destination, a platform lacking an atomic no-clobber rename primitive, or a rename expressed inside a unified patch.

What this means

  • The requested overwrite/resource type, no-replace rename primitive or patch rename form lies outside the supported implementation. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The requested overwrite/resource type, no-replace rename primitive or patch rename form lies outside the supported implementation.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the unsupported operation form or platform primitive before choosing a supported alternative.

How to fix it

  • Read the receipt message. Copy or move into a fresh destination instead of merging directories, perform renames with file.move rather than patch headers, and where the host lacks renameat2, renameatx_np or Windows no-replace rename, use an explicit copy followed by a verified delete (gateway_core/file_manage.copy/move/rename_no_replace, file_patch.parse_patch).
  • Use an operation advertised by the selected Gateway and platform.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The chosen supported operation preserves the intended overwrite, rename and metadata requirements.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass the unsupported-feature check or reinterpret an unsupported response as success.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
